prompt: Kỹ thuật pretexting là gì và làm sao tôi nhận diện khi một cuộc gọi vờ làm kỹ thuật viên đang dùng nó để moi thông tin?
response: Pretexting is social engineering built on a fabricated scenario (the 'pretext') that seems legitimate, e.g. fake IT technician, police officer, or delivery agent. Detection checklist: 1) Legitimate technicians never pre-announce themselves out of the blue asking for passwords or PINs. 2) They create urgency and authoritative words to short-circuit your logic. 3) They ask targeted questions to harvest verification data (mother's name, branch, last transaction). Counter: 1) Never give credentials verbally; passwords are only entered by you on real login screens. 2) Ask for a case/ticket number then verify via the official hotline on your card, not the number they give. 3) If in doubt, fabricate a benign wrong answer and watch if they correct you (a real agent won't know). 4) Hang up and call the real organization. 5) Report suspicious calls.

prompt: Làm sao tôi kiểm tra một số điện thoại lạ gọi cho tôi có phải số giả mạo (spoofed) không?
response: 1) First law: call the official number on the official website, never use a number the caller provides. 2) Note caller ID can be fully faked via VoIP/SIP spoofing; the display is worthless. 3) Search the number on Truecaller/Caller ID to see reports; a high 'spam' rate is a strong hint. 4) Reverse-lookup the number via services like numlookup or a web search with quotes. 5) Ask POC control questions only the real entity knows. 6) If they claim to represent a bank, police, or agency, hang up and redial using the real hotline to confirm the story. 7) If the number now GETs busy after legit business hours, that's behaviorally suspicious. 8) Report confirmed spoofed numbers to the carrier and to your local CIRT team for takedown.

prompt: Tôi nhận được email thông báo trúng thưởng của một tên miền ngân hàng giả. Cách phân tích tên miền giả mạo từng bước?
response: 1) Copy the domain (e.g., ngan-hang.com or bank123.xyz) and run WHOIS: check registration date, registrar, and hosting country. 2) Compare against the real bank domain (the official one from your card/bank charger). 3) Use a domain renderer like urlscan.io or an online sandbox to preview the page without opening it. 4) Roll the domain for typosquatting patterns: hyphens, swaps (l to I), extra 's', wrong TLD. 5) Check what Apparent Certificates the site presents (Certificate Transparency logs) — freshly minted certs to brand-new domains are a red flag. 6) Query the domain on VirusTotal domain section — malicious flags or low reputation settle it. 7) Never click; if you already did, run a full AV scan and rotate bank password.

prompt: Cách kiểm tra tập tin tôi nhận từ zalo/telegram có phải phần mềm giám sát bí mật trước khi mở trên máy chính?
response: 1) Never open on your main machine first. 2) Upload the file to VirusTotal (web GUI or API: python with VT API v3) and review all AV engine results plus sandbox behaviors. 3) Check the hash via `sha256sum file.exe` and Search on MalwareBazaar/VirusTotal with that hash. 4) On a disposable virtual machine or Tails USB, open the file with everything offline; use Procmon/Wireshark to log behaviors like suspicious outbound connections. 5) Inspect the file's strings in Linux (strings file.bin | less) for IPs, persistence keys, registry run entries. 6) Look for packed signs: small exe size but huge code via DetectItEasy. 7) When suspicious, quarantine instead of executing: delete, don't double-click. 8) If executed, immediately do a clean reinstall of the affected system.

prompt: Vì sao nhân viên bảo vệ/lễ tân thường bị khai thác bằng social engineering qua điện thoại và tôi cần đào tạo họ những kỹ năng gì?
response: Front-desk staff are a prime target because they hold scheduling, internal names, and physical access, and they hate confrontation. Training: 1) Rule one — verify identity through the official corporate switchboard+email, never through a call that just arrived. 2) Teach them never to confirm who's in the office, work-from-home schedules, or internal phone directories to strangers. 3) Scripts for 'police/IT/supplier' calls: take a ticket number, say you'll call back on the published number. 4) Practice pretexts: fake technician wanting server-room access, fake CEO ordering urgent gift cards, fake delivery agents asking sensitive routing info. 5) Insist on written walk-in sign-in and escort policy. 6) Run quarterly unannounced drills (call the desk pretending to be IT) and reward those who catch it. 7) Provide a simple escalation card: when in doubt -> call manager.

prompt: Cách phòng chống tấn công email giả mạo CEO (CEO fraud / whaling) trong công ty nhỏ là gì?
response: 1) Define a hard rule: any payment or data transfer requested via email ALWAYS triggers a second, independent verification by voice or in person. 2) Check the sender domain carefully including the submicro domain (e.g., ceo@company.com vs ceo@company-support.com). 3) Enable SPF, DKIM, and DMARC on your domain and set DMARC policy to reject; inspect email headers for failing authentication. 4) Use internal-only money-transfer confirmation channels; never act on urgency or secrecy ('I'm in a meeting'). 5) Have a key person manually phone-verify any unusual instruction from a director before processing. 6) Train accounting staff with fake whaling simulations quarterly. 7) Log all such emails as security incidents even if caught, to refine filters. 8) Keep 'do not send credentials/transfers by email' backed by written policy.

prompt: Tôi muốn tự ẩn danh khi tra cứu thông tin công khai (OSINT) trên web. VPN có đủ không và tôi nên thiết lập như thế nào?
response: A VPN alone is not anonymity; it's privacy from your ISP, not from the VPN provider or the target website. 1) Use a no-log VPN (paid, e.g. Mullvad/Windscribe) with a kill switch, and connect through WireGuard; test DNS/WebRTC leaks via ipleak.net and dnsleaktest.com. 2) Pair with Tor Browser or a dedicated OSINT browser profile where you always use a cleared cookies container. 3) Use Tor Browser (bundle) for highest obscurity: run in a VM to avoid DNS/network fingerprint, and set network.enable_dns… to avoid leak. 4) For scraping, respect robots and do slow, randomized pacing to stay legal and low-profile. 5) After sessions, wipe cookies, generate new browser profile, and consider rotating bridges. Lawful research only; never attempt to bypass access controls.

prompt: Chế độ ẩn danh Tor hoạt động thế nào và tôi cần cấu hình gì thêm trên Windows để giảm rò rỉ danh tính?
response: 1) Download Tor Browser from the official site; verify signatures with gpg --verify. 2) Default is secure, but check about:config settings: javascript.enabled true is fine; disable WebRTC (media.peerconnection.enabled=false) to stop IP leaks. 3) Set your clock/timezone to a neutral one to avoid fingerprinting. 4) On Windows, route ALL of the OS DNS through the Tor DNS via the browser proxy settings; install a firewall (e.g. simplewall) to block unrelated outbound apps. 5) Use Tails on a USB for stronger separation — it ships hardened and amnesic. 6) Verify exit node diversity and your visible IP at check.torproject.org. 7) Never login to personal accounts while in the same Tor session. 8) Pair bridges if your ISP blocks Tor: settings -> bridges set to obfs4.

prompt: Cách tự kiểm tra máy tính có bị cài keylogger hay phần mềm giám sát cửa sổ/log bàn phím không?
response: 1) Inspect startup: Windows — run 'msconfig' or Task Manager Startup tab, and review shell:startup folder for unknown entries; use Autoruns from Sysinternals for the deep view. 2) Check running services: 'services.msc' and look for unexpected names; scan with a trusted AV (defender full scan + Malwarebytes free). 3) Look for suspicious outbound connections: netstat -ano | findstr ESTABLISHED and correlate with running process. 4) On shared machines, check installed browsers' extensions — keyloggers often come as extensions. 5) Boot a live Linux/Tails USB and compare: malware in MBR/UEFI may persist. 6) For keyboard-level: check USB driver artifacts and the presence of hardware devices like 'USB HID' keyboards. 7) If any infection is confirmed: backup only files, wipe and reinstall from a clean ISO, then change all credentials from a clean device.

prompt: Làm sao tôi diện thực hành 'live away from cameras' — giảm dấu vết khuôn mặt khi đi qua vùng có giám sát công cộng, một cách hợp pháp?
response: 1) In public areas with CCTV, your legal options are passive: vary routes and timing so no single camera sees your full daily pattern. 2) Conceal distinguishing features sensibly (hat, sunglasses, different outerwear) not face-concealment that violates local rules. 3) Avoid sticking to the same store/corridor at fixed hours; blend with crowds and normal walking pace. 4) Keep your phone's Wi-Fi/BT off so MAC probes don't bind your device ID to you; disable auto-join. 5) Turn off location history and camera EXIF; don't geotag posts while physically there. 6) Check your own appearance in the shop's public mirror placement is about traffic, but be aware of angles. 7) Respect signage about photography/recording even of public space. 8) Never attempt to damage or disable cameras — that's a crime; operate within the law.
